slot.brief: List four ordering statements about first ionisation enthalpies across a period or down a group (including a Be/B or N/O type anomaly) and ask which statement is wrong.

stem: Which of the following orders of first ionisation enthalpy ($\Delta_i H_1$) is incorrect?

verdicts.working: IE1 (kJ/mol): B 801 < Be 900 < C 1086 < N 1402 (A ok); Al 578 < Mg 738 < Si 786 < P 1012 (B ok); I 1008 < Br 1140 < Cl 1251 < F 1681 (D ok). But N (1402, half-filled 2p3) > O (1314), so C < N < O < F fails.

working:
Across a period, first ionisation enthalpy generally increases with increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic radius, but with exceptions at fully filled and half-filled subshells:
1. Nitrogen ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^3$) has an extra-stable half-filled $2p$ subshell, whereas oxygen ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^4$) experiences inter-electronic repulsion in the doubly occupied $2p$ orbital. Consequently, $\Delta_i H_1(\text{N}) = 1402\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ is greater than $\Delta_i H_1(\text{O}) = 1314\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Thus, the correct increasing order of $\Delta_i H_1$ is $\text{C} < \text{O} < \text{N} < \text{F}$, making the order $\text{C} < \text{N} < \text{O} < \text{F}$ incorrect.

2. For the other options:
- $\text{B} (801\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{Be} (899\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{C} (1086\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{N} (1402\text{ kJ mol}^{-1})$ is correct because $\text{Be}$ ($2s^2$) has a fully filled subshell and higher penetration than $\text{B}$ ($2s^2 2p^1$).
- $\text{Al} (577\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{Mg} (737\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{Si} (786\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{P} (1012\text{ kJ mol}^{-1})$ is correct because $\text{Mg}$ ($3s^2$) has a fully filled subshell.
- $\text{I} (1008\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{Br} (1142\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{Cl} (1251\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}) < \text{F} (1681\text{ kJ mol}^{-1})$ is correct as ionisation enthalpy decreases down Group 17.

Independent check: IE1 (kJ/mol): B 801 < Be 900 < C 1086 < N 1402 (A ok); Al 578 < Mg 738 < Si 786 < P 1012 (B ok); I 1008 < Br 1140 < Cl 1251 < F 1681 (D ok). But N (1402, half-filled 2p3) > O (1314), so C < N < O < F fails.

draft.distractor_notes:
A: Trap for students who forget the Be/B anomaly and assume first ionisation enthalpy strictly increases with atomic number without exception.
B: Trap for students who forget the Mg/Al anomaly (fully filled $3s^2$ subshell in Mg gives it a higher $\Delta_i H_1$ than Al).
D: Trap for students who incorrectly assume ionisation enthalpy increases down a group due to the increase in total nuclear charge.
